New word

Coordinator

Source: MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology), Japan

Policy: how Japan built this support

1
2018–2022 (extended to 2024)
5-year ICT plan sets the funded level: 1 coordinator per 4 schools
2
August 2021
Job title and duties defined in national regulations
3
2025–2027
3-year plan keeps 1 per 4 schools and adds a help desk
Funding: local government finance, part of each municipality's general revenue → each municipality decides.
The ICT budget (more than ¥140 billion a year, 2025–27) covers the whole ICT environment, not coordinators alone.
Sources: MEXT, 3-year plan for school ICT environment (2025–2027); MEXT notice on the School Education Act Enforcement Regulations (23 Aug 2021)

Number of coordinators by fiscal year · ≈ schools per coordinator
7,178

1 per 4.5
schools, on average
about 75%
of municipalities have them; about 25% do not
The start-up phase is over: growth flattened after 2022 (7,144 → 7,178).
Next: municipalities with none, and the quality of support.
Source: MEXT, survey of ICT-related finances of schools (end of FY2024). Counts may be incomplete where municipalities outsource the work.
That was my job in Obuse.
ICT Coordinator, 2020–2024
Photo: author’s own, Obuse
Four areas of work
Source: author’s own work as ICT Coordinator in Obuse, 2020–2024

Lesson support

  • Team teaching: Grade 2 math
  • Lesson consultation: Grade 9 music

School administration support

  • School administration DX: a simple in-house system
  • Class lists: yearly update
  • Account setup and registration

Equipment and environment

  • Device-use rules, decided with the Board of Education
  • Annual update: accounts, device reset
  • Quick response when devices fail

In-school training

  • Beginner-level courses on using the tools
  • Sharing examples of practice from lessons in other schools
Being in the school made the support useful.

One form of this future: multi-track instruction

Single-track (one-way)
Teacher Gives the same input and instructions to everyone.
Learners Same activity, same pace, same place. Little choice.
Multi-track (interactive)
Teacher Short input, then sees each child’s progress and advises one by one.
Learners Choose their own pace and place. Look at each other’s work, from the blank page and in progress (peer referencing).
Source: Jun Takahashi, “Realizing multi-track instruction” (note, 24 Jul 2025). Illustrations drawn by the author.

Obuse: the Town of Chestnuts, Hokusai and Flowers

Chestnuts
Chestnut sweets, and orchards of apples and grapes
Hokusai
Hokusai stayed here in his 80s. The Hokusai-kan museum opened in 1976.
Flowers
Open gardens: residents welcome visitors into their own gardens
